nodes.title: the Umbtu signature
nodes.statement: The Umbtu system concerns objects called drigrixs. There are exactly 5 of them: solvex, umbazt, glimmux, vashtez, qenvex. Two operations are written @ and +. One relation is written ::, read as "covers".

nodes.title: the Umbtu combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x @ y for every pair of drigrixs is fixed by the table of the first operation, and likewise for +. The pairs standing in the :: relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all drigrixs x and y, x @ y is again a drigrix.

nodes.title: association of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all drigrixs x, y, z: (x @ y) @ z = x @ (y @ z).

nodes.title: commutation of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all drigrixs x and y: x @ y = y @ x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a drigrix solvex with solvex @ x = x @ solvex = x for every x.

nodes.title: an absorbing object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a drigrix qenvex with qenvex @ x = x @ qenvex = qenvex for every x.

nodes.title: closure under the second operation
nodes.statement: For all drigrixs x and y, x + y is again a drigrix.

nodes.title: association of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all drigrixs x, y, z: (x + y) + z = x + (y + z).

nodes.title: commutation of the second operation
nodes.statement: For all drigrixs x and y: x + y = y + x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the second operation
nodes.statement: There is a drigrix qenvex with qenvex + x = x for every x.

nodes.title: self combination under the second operation
nodes.statement: For every drigrix x: x + x = x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all drigrixs x and y: if x :: y and y :: x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all drigrixs x, y, z: if x :: y and y :: z then x :: z.

nodes.title: the system does not have reversal under the first operation
nodes.statement: Some drigrix x admits no drigrix y for which x @ y and y @ x both land on a neutral object.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = umbazt, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: opalrast drigrixs
nodes.statement: A drigrix x is called opalrast when x @ x = x.

nodes.title: drigrixs that korrhob
nodes.statement: Two drigrixs x and y are said to korrhob when x @ y = y @ x.

nodes.title: vexfex collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of drigrixs is vexfex when x @ y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the aztdri of a drigrix
nodes.statement: The aztdri of a drigrix x is the collection of drigrixs y for which x :: y holds.

nodes.title: the mornvint
nodes.statement: The drigrix solvex is called the mornvint of the system. It is the unique drigrix that leaves every drigrix unchanged under @.

nodes.title: the kapon
nodes.statement: The kapon of the system is the collection of drigrixs that korrhob with every drigrix.

nodes.title: the tezjen
nodes.statement: The tezjen is the collection of all opalrast drigrixs.

nodes.title: the vintmux of a drigrix
nodes.statement: The vintmux of a drigrix x, written [x], is the smallest vexfex collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a grixvash
nodes.statement: A drigrix f is a grixvash when f :: y holds for every drigrix y, that is, when the aztdri of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: qennyr drigrixs
nodes.statement: A drigrix x is qennyr when x @ x equals the mornvint.

nodes.title: the mornzam of a drigrix
nodes.statement: The mornzam of a drigrix x is the number of drigrixs in its vintmux [x].

nodes.title: the rastdri
nodes.statement: The rastdri of the system is the collection of drigrixs whose mornzam is largest.

nodes.title: nakkeld pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct drigrixs x and y form a nakkeld pair when x :: y and y :: x both hold, that is, when each lies in the aztdri of the other.

nodes.title: the mornvint is the only one of its kind
nodes.statement: There is exactly one drigrix e with e @ x = x @ e = x for every drigrix x.

verification.domain: every object paired with every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose e and f both leave every drigrix unchanged.
Then e @ f = f, reading e as neutral on the left.
And e @ f = e, reading f as neutral on the right.
So e = f, and the two suppositions describe the same object.

nodes.title: the mornvint lies in the kapon
nodes.statement: The mornvint korrhobs with every drigrix.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let e be the mornvint and x any drigrix.
Then e @ x = x and x @ e = x.
So e @ x = x @ e, which is what it means to korrhob.
Since x was arbitrary, e belongs to the kapon.

nodes.title: the kapon is vexfex
nodes.statement: If x and y both korrhob with every drigrix, then so does x @ y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y lie in the kapon and let z be any drigrix.
Then (x @ y) @ z = x @ (y @ z).
Move z past y, then past x, using that each korrhobs with everything.
So x @ y korrhobs with z, and the kapon is vexfex.

nodes.title: the vintmux of a drigrix is vexfex
nodes.statement: For every drigrix x, the collection [x] is vexfex.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under @.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the vintmux is contained in every vexfex collection
nodes.statement: If S is vexfex and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a drigrix is opalrast exactly when its mornzam is one
nodes.statement: x @ x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x @ x = x then {x} is already closed under @.
So [x] = {x} and the mornzam is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x @ x, which is then x.

nodes.title: where the mornzam divides the number of drigrixs breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every drigrix x, the mornzam of x divides 5.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = umbazt, reach = 4, size = 5, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the vintmux of a kapon drigrix stays in the kapon
nodes.statement: If x lies in the kapon then every drigrix of [x] lies in the kapon.

verification.domain: every object of the core, then its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The kapon is vexfex.
[x] is the smallest vexfex collection containing x.
A smallest such collection sits inside any other, and the kapon is one.

nodes.title: the tezjen is vexfex
nodes.statement: If x and y are both opalrast then so is x @ y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be opalrast.
The claim asks whether (x @ y) @ (x @ y) returns x @ y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: aztdris are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the aztdri of x, then the aztdri of y is contained in the aztdri of x.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x :: y and let z satisfy y :: z.
Transitivity gives x :: z.
So every member of the aztdri of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one grixvash
nodes.statement: No two distinct drigrixs can both be grixvashs.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f :: h, since h is any object, and h :: f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: no nakkeld pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct drigrixs lie in each other's aztdri.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.

nodes.title: every drigrix lies in the kapon
nodes.statement: Every pair of drigrixs korrhobs.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The kapon is defined by korrhobing with everything.
The claim is that x @ y = y @ x for every pair.
That is settled by scanning the table for a pair that disagrees.

nodes.title: the second operation keeps the kapon intact
nodes.statement: If x and y lie in the kapon then so does x + y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The kapon is already vexfex under @.
The second operation is defined on every pair.
The claim is that + respects the kapon as well.
